1: ## 1. Project Setup & Build Infrastructure

12: ## 2. Core Graph Model
13: 
14: - [x] 2.1 Define `NodeId`, `EdgeId`, `CommunityId` as strong typedefs (type-safe integer wrappers)
15: - [x] 2.2 Implement `struct Node` with id, name, adjacency list, groups, assignment state (true/false/unassigned), activity counter, appearance counts
16: - [x] 2.3 Implement `struct Edge` with source/target NodeId, bidirectional flag, weight, visibility state, type (normal/conflict)
17: - [x] 2.4 Implement `struct Clause` as set of (NodeId, polarity) pairs using `std::unordered_map<NodeId, bool>`
18: - [x] 2.5 Implement template `class Graph<NodeT, EdgeT>` with operations: createNode, createEdge, connect, getNode, getNodes, getEdges, getClauses, removeNode, removeEdge
19: - [x] 2.6 Implement `CommunityNode` extending Node with community ID and bridge flag
20: - [x] 2.7 Implement `CommunityGraph` extending Graph with community statistics (Q modularity, community sizes, edge ratios, inter/intra community edges)
21: - [x] 2.8 Implement CSR (Compressed Sparse Row) adjacency structure for performance-critical paths
22: - [x] 2.9 Implement Union-Find (disjoint set) for connectivity queries with path compression and union by rank

26: ## 3. DIMACS CNF Parser
27: 
28: - [x] 3.1 Implement `dimacs::Parser` class with `parse(file_path, mode)` returning a Graph
29: - [x] 3.2 Implement p-line parsing (`p cnf <vars> <clauses>`) with error handling for missing/duplicate problem lines
30: - [x] 3.3 Implement c-line parsing for variable naming (`c <id> <name>`)
31: - [x] 3.4 Implement regex-based variable grouping from named variables (user-provided regex patterns)
32: - [x] 3.5 Implement clause line parsing (space-separated literals, terminated by 0, multi-line clauses)
33: - [x] 3.6 Implement VIG mode: create edges between variables co-occurring in same clause, edge weight = co-occurrence count
34: - [x] 3.7 Implement LIG mode: create edges between signed literals, preserving polarity in node identity
35: - [x] 3.8 Implement progress reporting callback (byte position / file size → 0.0 to 1.0)

39: ## 4. Community Detection
40: 
41: - [x] 4.1 Create `community::Detector` interface with virtual method `detect(Graph&) -> CommunityResult`
42: - [x] 4.2 Implement community factory: register detectors by name ("louvain", "cnm", "online")
43: - [x] 4.3 Implement Louvain detector wrapping `igraph_community_louvain` — convert Graph to igraph graph, run algorithm, extract partition + Q modularity
44: - [x] 4.4 Implement CNM detector wrapping `igraph_community_fastgreedy` — same conversion flow
45: - [x] 4.5 Implement Online (OL) community detector — custom incremental assignment (~300 lines based on satlib OLCommunityMetric.java)
46: - [x] 4.6 Implement disjoint graph detection: warn and handle gracefully when Louvain encounters disconnected components
47: - [x] 4.7 Implement community statistics computation: min/max/mean/SD of community sizes, inter/intra community edge counts, edge ratio
48: - [x] 4.8 Write unit tests with known community structures, verify Q modularity ranges, test disjoint graph handling

50: ## 5. Layout Engine (CPU)
51: 
52: - [x] 5.1 Create `layout::Layout` interface with virtual method `compute(Graph&, progress_callback) -> CoordinateMap`
53: - [x] 5.2 Implement layout factory: register by short name ("f", "forceAtlas2", "kk", "c", "grid", "gkk")
54: - [x] 5.3 Implement Fruchterman-Reingold CPU layout: O(n²) per iteration, configurable iterations (default 500), cooling schedule, optimal distance k = C * sqrt(area/n), rescaling to bounds
55: - [x] 5.4 Implement Kamada-Kawai layout: all-pairs shortest-path based, handle disconnected components separately
56: - [x] 5.5 Implement ForceAtlas2 layout: multi-threaded, Barnes-Hut optimization (theta=1.2), auto-adjusted speed, lin-log mode, gravity, edge weight influence
57: - [x] 5.6 Implement Community Circular layout: place community centers on circle, run FR within each community
58: - [x] 5.7 Implement Community Grid layout: arrange communities in 2D grid, FR within each cell
59: - [x] 5.8 Implement Community Grid+KK hybrid: grid for community placement, KK for intra-community
60: - [x] 5.9 Implement Community ForceAtlas2: run FA2 on quotient graph, then FR within communities
61: - [x] 5.10 Implement progress reporting (0.0 to 1.0) for all layouts
62: - [x] 5.11 Write unit tests: verify all layouts produce coordinates for every node, no NaN/inf, coordinates within bounds, factory returns correct types

64: ## 6. Layout Engine (GPU / OpenCL)
65: 
66: - [x] 6.1 Create OpenCL context initialization: enumerate platforms, find AMD device, create context + command queue
67: - [x] 6.2 Port FR repulsion kernel from Java OpenCL to C OpenCL kernel source
68: - [x] 6.3 Port FR attraction kernel from Java OpenCL to C OpenCL kernel source
69: - [x] 6.4 Port FR aggregation and position adjustment kernels
70: - [x] 6.5 Implement GPU FR placer: upload graph data to OpenCL buffers, run kernel pipeline, read back positions
71: - [x] 6.6 Implement CPU fallback when OpenCL is unavailable (detect at runtime, emit warning, delegate to CPU FR)
72: - [x] 6.7 Register "fgpu" in layout factory
73: - [x] 6.8 Write integration test: GPU FR on small graph, compare output quality with CPU FR; test fallback path

75: ## 7. SAT Solver Integration
76: 
77: - [x] 7.1 Implement `solver::ExternalSolver` class: spawn solver binary as child process, pass CNF file and FIFO path as arguments
78: - [x] 7.2 Implement named FIFO creation (`mkfifo`) with RAII cleanup (remove FIFO on destruction)
79: - [x] 7.3 Implement solver process lifecycle management: start, monitor (detect SAT exit code 10 / UNSAT exit code 20), stop (SIGTERM on user cancel)
80: - [x] 7.4 Implement crash handling: detect unexpected process termination, report error, clean up FIFO and pipes
81: - [x] 7.5 Add CLI option `-s <solver_path>` — mandatory for evolution mode, error if missing
82: - [x] 7.6 Add GUI file selector for solver binary path, persist selection in application settings
83: - [x] 7.7 Write unit tests: launch a mock solver script that writes known events to FIFO, verify FIFO IPC end-to-end, verify cleanup on normal/crash exit

85: ## 8. Evolution Engine
86: 
87: - [x] 8.1 Define event types: VariableAssignment (id, state, activity), ClauseEvent (add/remove, literal IDs), ConflictEvent (conflict number)
88: - [x] 8.2 Implement event stream parser: parse 'v', 'c', '!' lines from pipe/callback into typed events
89: - [x] 8.3 Implement forward evolution: apply events sequentially, update node/edge states in graph
90: - [x] 8.4 Implement backward evolution: maintain state history stack, revert to previous state
91: - [x] 8.5 Implement file buffering: split solver output into ~1M line chunks, buffer next file in background thread
92: - [x] 8.6 Implement conflict scanning: jump to specific conflict number by forward/backward replay
93: - [x] 8.7 Implement decision variable tracking: highlight current decision variable, clear on next decision
94: - [x] 8.8 Implement observer pattern: registered observers receive nodeAssigned, addEdge, removeEdge, updateGraph, newFileReady callbacks
95: - [x] 8.9 Support both VIG and LIG graph modes during evolution
96: - [x] 8.10 Write unit tests: parse sample event stream, verify forward/backward state transitions, verify conflict scanning lands on correct state

98: ## 9. Rendering Layer
99: 
100: - [x] 9.1 Create `rendering::GraphRenderer` class wrapping QGraphicsScene
101: - [x] 9.2 Implement node rendering: circles with configurable diameter (default 10px), community-based color palette
102: - [x] 9.3 Implement edge rendering: lines with community coloring (intra=community color, inter=white/gray), conflict edge style
103: - [x] 9.4 Implement layered rendering: edge layer (bottom), node layer, highlight layer, decision variable layer (top)
104: - [x] 9.5 Implement multi-threaded draw: distribute edge/node drawing across threads, batch-add to scene on main thread
105: - [x] 9.6 Implement double buffering for flicker-free redraws
106: - [x] 9.7 Implement zoom via QGraphicsView transform, pan via scroll bars and mouse drag
107: - [x] 9.8 Implement node click detection via QGraphicsItem hit testing
108: - [x] 9.9 Implement scale-aware rendering: hide labels at low zoom, show at high zoom, simplify edges at low zoom
109: - [x] 9.10 Implement visibility filters: show/hide by community, assignment state, edge type
110: - [x] 9.11 Implement community highlight layer: outline or shade community regions
111: - [x] 9.12 Write integration tests: render a 10K-node graph, verify layers, verify click detection, verify filter toggling

113: ## 10. GUI (Qt 6 + QML)
114: 
115: - [x] 10.1 Create QML main window with split pane layout: canvas (left ~70%) + control panel (right ~30%), resizable divider
116: - [x] 10.2 Implement menu bar: File (Open, Save, Export), View (zoom in/out/fit/reset), Help (About)

result.content:
1: ## Context
2: 
3: satGraf is a Java SAT solver visualization tool (~100 Java source files + satlib.jar with 66 classes). The system parses DIMACS CNF files, builds variable interaction graphs, detects communities, computes force-directed layouts, and renders interactively. The Java codebase has been fully analyzed and decompiled:
4: 
5: - **satlib.jar**: Core graph model (Graph/Node/Edge/Clause), DIMACS parsing (DimacsGraphFactory), community detection (LouvianNetwork ~877 lines, CNM, OL), evolution tracking (Evolution ~728 lines)
6: - **satgraf**: Layout algorithms (FruchPlacer, ForceAtlas2, FruchGPUPlacer with OpenCL kernels), Swing UI (GraphCanvas with EdgeLayer/NodeLayer/HighlightLayer), export (JPEG/GIF)
7: - **Dependencies**: 32 JAR files including JUNG, Gephi layout, JOCL (OpenCL), Trove (primitive collections), JFreeChart, commons-cli
8: 
9: The rewrite targets C++17/20 with igraph replacing custom community detection, Qt 6 replacing Swing, native OpenCL replacing JOCL, and external solver binary integration replacing the original minisat process spawning.
10: 
11: ## Goals / Non-Goals
12: 
13: **Goals:**
14: - Order-of-magnitude performance improvement for layout computation on large graphs (100K+ variables)
15: - GPU-accelerated layout via OpenCL on AMD iGPU (no CUDA dependency)
16: - Modern, visually appealing Qt 6 + QML GUI
17: - Feature parity with original satGraf (all modes: com/imp/evo/exp)
18: - Clean, modular C++ architecture with clear separation of computation and rendering
19: - External SAT solver integration via named pipe IPC for evolution tracking
20: - Headless CLI export mode for batch processing
21: 
22: **Non-Goals:**
23: - Java interoperability or JNI bridge
24: - Backward compatibility with satlib.jar data formats (except DIMACS CNF)
25: - Windows/macOS support in initial release (Linux primary, cross-platform later)
26: - Web-based visualization (future consideration)
27: - Real-time collaborative editing
28: - Bundling or embedding any specific SAT solver (user supplies their own binary)
29: 
30: ## Decisions
31: 
32: ### Decision 1: igraph for community detection (not custom implementation)
33: 
34: **Choice**: Use igraph C library for Louvain and CNM community detection.
35: 
36: **Rationale**: The original satlib.jar contains ~1200 lines of custom Louvain (LouvianNetwork.java) and CNM implementations. igraph provides these as battle-tested, optimized C functions (`igraph_community_louvain`, `igraph_community_fastgreedy`). This eliminates the largest algorithmic porting effort and provides better performance.
37: 
38: **Alternative considered**: Port LouvianNetwork.java directly to C++. Rejected because igraph's implementation is faster (SIMD-optimized), handles edge cases better (disjoint graphs), and is actively maintained.
39: 
40: **Trade-off**: Adds igraph as a dependency (~2MB). The Online (OL) community detection algorithm is not in igraph and must be custom-implemented (~300 lines).
41: 
42: ### Decision 2: Qt 6 + QML for GUI (not Dear ImGui or GTK)
43: 
44: **Choice**: Qt 6 with QGraphicsScene for canvas rendering and QML for control panels.
45: 
46: **Rationale**: QGraphicsScene/QGraphicsView is purpose-built for rendering thousands of items with GPU acceleration, spatial indexing for hit testing, and built-in zoom/pan. QML provides modern declarative UI for control panels. No other framework matches this combination for graph visualization.
47: 
48: **Alternative considered**: Dear ImGui (too tool-like, not "modern beautiful"), GTK (less mature GPU rendering), egui (Rust-only).
49: 
50: **Trade-off**: Qt is a large dependency. CMake integration is well-established. Licensing is LGPL/Commercial.
51: 
52: ### Decision 3: OpenCL for GPU compute (not CUDA, not Vulkan compute, not wgpu)
53: 
54: **Choice**: Native OpenCL C API for GPU-accelerated Fruchterman-Reingold layout.
55: 
56: **Rationale**: The user has AMD integrated graphics. CUDA is NVIDIA-only. The existing FruchGPUPlacer.java already contains working OpenCL kernels (repel, attract, adjust, aggregate) that can be ported directly to C OpenCL calls. Vulkan compute and wgpu would require rewriting all kernels.
57: 
58: **Alternative considered**: Vulkan compute (more modern but massive rewrite of kernels), wgpu (Rust-first, C++ bindings immature).
59: 
60: **Trade-off**: OpenCL is older but proven. AMD's OpenCL driver support is solid. The existing kernels are OpenCL — direct port is lowest risk.
61: 
62: ### Decision 4: External solver binary via named pipe (not embedded library)
63: 
64: **Choice**: The user provides a solver binary path via `-s <path>`. The application launches it as an external process and communicates via a named pipe (FIFO) to capture solver events.
65:
